Judgment

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 08.08.2023 at about 9.00 pm., when the petitioner was waiting for the bus on extreme left side of (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.5806/2023 the Service road, outer ring road, near Marathahalli multiplex, at that time, a Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and property, dashed against the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner sustained multiple injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, foods and nourishment.
The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 by its driver.
The Airport Traffic police have registered a case in crime No.203/2023 under Section 279, 337 of IPC.
The first respondent being the owner and the second respondent being the insurer of the Lorry are jointly and severally are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

After service of summons, the respondent No.1 and the respondent No.2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their objections to the main petition.
4.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts of the same.
He has contended that, his vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent and as on the date of accident the policy, permit and DL are valid at the time of accident.
He had denied the nature of accident and involvement of the lorry.
With these grounds the respondent No.1 sought for rejecting the claim petition.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts of the same.

Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the lorry regarding the driving (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.5806/2023 licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory Abhishek K vs Ganesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130288236/
2 provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
It has contented that, at the time of accident, the driver of the Lorry does not posses valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.

It has contended that, the tanker in question did not hold valid permit and FC as on the date of accident, whereas the first respondent obtained the permit from the authority on 09.10.2023 and it is valid up to 8.10.2028 under ie., after the accident.
It has admitted the issuance of the policy in respect of Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40- 5789.
Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of the Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 in the alleged accident.

Further contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself as the petitioner was crossing the road in a place not meant for pedestrian crossing and was crossing the road carelessly (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.5806/2023 and thereby caused the accident.
Further contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful.
With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for rejecting the claim petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner prove that, on 08.08.2023 at about 9.00 pm., the claimant was waiting for the bus on extreme left side of the service road, outer ring road, near Marathahalli Multiplex, at that time, the driver of Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to tremendous impact he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the alleged RTA ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.

In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.5806/2023 examined as PW.1, Dr. Deepu.N.K has examined as PW.2 and MRD Technician at Manipal Hospitals has examined as PW.3 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.19.
On the other hand, State Head Legal has examined as RW.1 and the Superintendent, RTO, K R Puram has examined as RW.2 and in all got marked Ex.R.1 to 6 and closed their side evidence.
7. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.

The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the following citations reported in :
1. 2018 ACJ 1768 2. 2020 ACJ 2560 3. MFA 202104/24 Abhishek K vs Ganesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130288236/
3 4. SLP (c) 10351/2019 5. AIR 2019 SC 999 8.

My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
 (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.5806/2023  -:R E A S O N S:-
9. Issue No.1:-

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 08.08.2023 at about 9.00 pm.,
when he was waiting for the bus on extreme left side of the Service road, outer ring road, near Marathahalli multiplex, at that time, a Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and property, dashed against him.
Due to said impact, the he sustained multiple injuries all over the body.
10. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief-examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.

He also got marked Ex.P1 to P13 which are FIR, complaint, wound certificate, panchanama, IMV report, sketch, chargesheet, Aadhar card, marks cards,
discharge summary, lab report and medical bills.
11. I have perused police documents which are marked at Ex-P1 to Ex-P7.

From these documents it is (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.5806/2023 clear that the accident took place on 08.08.2023 at about 9.00 am., and Ex.P.1 - FIR in crime No.0203/2023 came to be registered on 09.08.2023 at 20.00 i.e., on next day of accident at Airport Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 134(a&b) 187 of MV Act and 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 - complaint lodged by petitioner himself on 09.08.2023.
Ex.P.4 is the spot panchanama which shows the scene of offence.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV report discloses the right side bumper scrath caused to the vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789.

Ex.P.6 is the rough sketch and Ex.P.7 is the chargesheet which was registered against driver of the offending Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 for the offences punishable under Section 187, 134(a&b) of MV Act and 279, 338 of IPC.
12.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In his cross-examination he has specifically denied the suggestions Abhishek K vs Ganesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130288236/
4 made by the learned (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.5806/2023 counsel for the respondent regarding, by his own negligence the alleged accident occurred.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law

that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of the offending Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
(SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.5806/2023 13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one:
a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering:

The petitioner has contended due to accident he was sustained post traumatic injuries of forehead with underlying frontal bone fracture, (type-II anterior wall, extending to right supra orbital rim), degloving injury of right heel with fracture of calcaneum and fracture of tip of medial malleolus and other injuries.

He underwent wound debridement of forehead and right foot, open reduction and internal fixation of frontal bone using titanium mesh, (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.5806/2023 wound debridement for degloving injury of right heel, wound debridement + free left latissmus dorsi muscle flap for right foot, SSG on LD muscle flap under GA.
In order to prove injuries caused to him, he has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P3 which reveals that petitioner has sustained simple as well as grevious injuries.
Further, Petitioner examined one MRO as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.16.
Petitioner has also examined Dr.Deepu.N.K as PW.2 and got marked outpatient file at Ex.P.14 and X-ray marked at Ex.P.15.
PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses:

Petitioner has produced 28 medical bills amounting to Rs.8,17,837/-
which are marked at Ex.P.13 and the respondent No.2 has (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.5806/2023 not elicited anything to disprove the same.
Therefore it is just and reasonable to award in all Rs.8,17,837/- under the head medical expenses.

Abhishek K vs Ganesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130288236/
5
c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges:
PW.1 has deposed that, immediately after accident he took treatment as an inpatient at Manipal Hospital from 09.08.2023 to 21.08.2023 i.e., for 13 days as per discharge summary marked at Ex.P.11.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 13 days and by including expenses of attendant of petitioner during the period of treatment and also by including conveyance, in all a sum of Rs.16,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment,
conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:
The petitioner contended that he was a MCA Graduate and (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.5806/2023 he was searching for job.

Therefore, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Accordingly, the fixed notional income of the year 2023 at 16,000/- p.m., Petitioner may took 2 months rest and he may lost income for those rest periods.
Therefore, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is entitled to Rs.32,000/- (Rs.16,000/- x 2) towards loss of income during treatment period.
e) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he was inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.

The petitioner also examined Dr.Deepu.N.K, working as plastic surgeon at HOSMAT Hospital as PW.2 and he has contended that, petitioner sustained degloving injury of right heal with fracture of calcaneum and fracture tip of (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.5806/2023 medial malleolus.

Further contended that, accordingly to the discharge summary,
petitioner had a severe head injury and a degloving in Manipal Hospital for both injuries. PW.2 examined right ankle and foot of petitioner wherein it is noticed lattissimus dorsi flap with skin gract in situ over right ankle and heel, a large area of 15 x 12 cm size skin graft which is insensate, stiff ankle joint on right side with minimum ankle joint movements.
PW.2 also noticed right thigh: donor site scar of skin harvested, back: long scar over the back and scar of 6 x 0.3 cm over forehead.

PW.2 assessed total permanent partial disability for the right lower limb at 55.23%
and to the whole body at 18.41%.

During cross examination PW.2 has deposed that,    
.

Abhishek K vs Ganesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130288236/
6
It is relevant to note that according to PW.2 has assessed total permanent partial disability for the right lower limb at 55.23% and to the whole body at 18.41%.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 16% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
PW.2 got marked outpatient file and X-ray at Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15.

Petitioner has also examined M R D Technician at Manipal Hospitals, Old Airport road, Bengaluru as PW.3 and through him got marked authorisation letter at Ex.P.18 and inpatient record marked at Ex.P.19.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 - Aadhar card in order to prove his age.
As per said document, he was born on 01.06.1995 and as on date of accident he was aged about 28 years.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 28 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "17" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
16,000 x 12 x 17 x 16% = Rs.5,22,240/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.5,22,240/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
f) Towards deprivation of Future Amenities:
T h e d oc tor h as opined that the pe titio ne r sustaine d (S CCH-9) 1 8 MVC.No.5806/2023 grievous injuries and he is unable do his day to day activities as earlier.

PW.2 deposed that, on examination petitioner complains of pain in right lower limb on standing for long period, difficulty in squatting, climbing stairs,
repeated ulcers on right foot, there is no sensation in right heel area over the flap and stiffness of right ankle and foot.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 has not contended about future medication to the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future medical expenses which shall not carry any interest.

14. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

15.

Regarding Liability: The respondent No.2 has taken contention that, the tanker in question did not hold valid permit and FC as on the date of accident, whereas the first respondent obtained the permit from the authority on 09.10.2023 and it is valid up to 8.10.2028 under ie., after the accident.

In support of it, Insurance company has examined its State Head Legal as RW.1 and through him (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.5806/2023 got marked authorisation letter at Ex.R.1, insurance policy at Ex.R.2 and permit at Ex.R.3 and also examined the Superintendent, RTO, K.R.Puram as RW.2 and through him got marked authorisation letter at Ex.R.4, permit extract at Ex.R.5 and RC extract at Ex.R.6.

On perusal of Ex.R.5 it came to know that, the vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 got permit on 09.10.2023 ie., after the accident and the vehicle is having validity of the permit from 09.10.2023 to 08.10.2028.
It shows that, there is gross violation of policy condition by the owner of the Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 as the offending vehicle not having valid permit as on the date of accident.

The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the citation reported in 2018 ACJ 1768 (Amrit Paul Singh and another Vs. Tata AIG General Ins. Co., Ltd., and others) wherein it is held that:
" Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Section 149(2)(a)(i)(c) read with section 66 - Motor Insurance - Permit - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.5806/2023 order - Tribunal found that offending truck was being plied without valid permit and directed insurance company to pay and recover - Order of the tribunal was confirmed by the High Court - Onus lies on the insured to prove possession of permit -

sentences.text:
No evidence produced by insured to prove that he had a permit to ply the vehicle on the date of accident - Use of transport vehicle in a public place without a permit is a fundamental statutory infraction - Whether the High Court and Abhishek K vs Ganesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130288236/
8 Tribunal were justified in directing the insurance company to pay compensation amount and then recover the same from owner and driver - Held: yes".
same point is considered in the citation reported in 2020 ACJ 2560 (New India Assurance Co. Ltd.,
Vs. Yallavva and another) wherein it is held that:
" Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Section 149(2)(a) and (b) read with section 149 (a), 149 (4) and 149(7) - Motor Insurance - Act or comprehensive policy - Breach of - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover order - In a case where insurance company successfully establishes that insured had committed breach of policy as per section 149 (2) (a) and breach was fundamental contributing to the cause of accident or policy is void as per section 149(2)(b), whether in view of the mandate under section 149(1) insurance company would be liable to satisfy the award vis-a-vis third party and entitled to recover the amount from the insured

sentences.text: - Held: yes; however if court comes to a finding that third party has played fraud or was in collusion with the insured for (SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.5806/2023 wrongful gain to themselves then court may exercise its discretion not to fasten liability on insurance company".
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the Insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2 Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.1.

The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order and the petitioner is entitled for 6% interest on the compensation amount of .14,48,077/- from the date of petition till realisation.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
 (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.5806/2023  ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .14,48,077/-
 (Rupees fourteen lakhs forty eight  thousand seventy seven only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 - Insurer shall pay the compensation amount with interest at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.1 - Owner.
The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City (SCCH-9) 24 MVC.No.5806/2023 Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 16% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future medical expenses which shall not carry any interest.
It shows that, there is gross violation of policy condition by the owner of the Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-40-5789 as the offending vehicle not having valid permit as on the date of accident.
No evidence produced by insured to prove that he had a permit to ply the vehicle on the date of accident - Use of transport vehicle in a public place without a permit is a fundamental statutory infraction - Whether the High Court and Abhishek K vs Ganesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130288236/
8 Tribunal were justified in directing the insurance company to pay compensation amount and then recover the same from owner and driver - Held: yes".
same point is considered in the citation reported in 2020 ACJ 2560 (New India Assurance Co. Ltd.,
Vs. Yallavva and another) wherein it is held that:
" Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Section 149(2)(a) and (b) read with section 149 (a), 149 (4) and 149(7) - Motor Insurance - Act or comprehensive policy - Breach of - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover order - In a case where insurance company successfully establishes that insured had committed breach of policy as per section 149 (2) (a) and breach was fundamental contributing to the cause of accident or policy is void as per section 149(2)(b), whether in view of the mandate under section 149(1) insurance company would be liable to satisfy the award vis-a-vis third party and entitled to recover the amount from the insured
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2 Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.1.
